headline: JPMorgan chief Jamie Dimon says builders of AI data centres should look to states that have spare electricity and welcome the projects.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score; the quotes are confirmed in the Times of India report, but the Firstpost wording on the 'biggest challenge' could not be checked.
importance_line: Communities near planned data centres and the companies building them are affected, since power supply and local opposition shape where the buildings go, but this is a bank chief's advice, not a policy or a measured shortfall.
source: The Times of India, citing a Bloomberg TV interview
summary: The Times of India reports, citing a Bloomberg TV interview, that JPMorgan Chase chief Jamie Dimon said "there are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power", advising data centre builders to choose places with electricity and local support rather than push into areas that object. In the same interview he said AI risks "went up 10-fold after Mythos", Anthropic's model, but that he will not "get hysterical" about whether AI is existential.
notes: Pool source Firstpost blocked; read The Times of India on the same interview. Interview date not stated.
